name: 2-foundations
title: Foundations: Kinds and Common
subtitle: Before the layers: the #Tag keywords every layer uses, and the definitions every layer shares — the items that flow, the ports and interfaces they cross, and the measures of effectiveness.

steps.label: SHOW ONLY THE KINDS PACKAGE
steps.text: ⊞ on Kinds shows only it in the diagrams. Kinds declares the #Tag keywords the model uses: layer, role, mode and lifecycle tags.

steps.label: GENERAL VIEW
steps.text: One metadata definition per tag: the five layers, then Mission, Actor, Mode, Hazard, MoE, Budget and more. The other packages write them as #MoE, #Hazard…

steps.label: TREE VIEW
steps.text: Tree shows what Kinds contains: its 33 tags and nothing else. General and Tree are the only views that show anything for Kinds.

steps.label: SHOW ONLY COMMON
steps.text: ⊞ on Common. It holds what every layer shares: the items that flow, the ports and interfaces they cross, and the measures of effectiveness.

steps.label: TREE VIEW
steps.text: Its 116 members hang off one package. Zoomed in: each measure of effectiveness, an «attribute», is followed by the «constraint» holding it to its target.

steps.label: GENERAL VIEW
steps.text: Definitions as boxes, attributes listed inside. Selected, CoordinationMessage is the hub: eight message kinds specialise it, so one mesh port carries them all.

steps.label: PUT AN ATTRIBUTE BACK
steps.text: Before recording we deleted sequenceNumber from CoordinationMessage, which now lists only senderId and sentAt. Now we add it back.

steps.label: PLACE AN ATTRIBUTE
steps.text: Pick Attribute in the palette, then click the definition box: a new attribute is created inside it and selected, ready to name.

steps.label: NAME IT AND TYPE IT
steps.text: In Properties: the name sequenceNumber, then the type ScalarValues::Integer, from the standard library; Enter binds it. The box lists it as name : type.

steps.label: DOCUMENT IT
steps.text: The documentation goes in the same panel, word for word as before: where the message sits in the sender's stream.

do.type: Where it sits in the sender's stream, so loss over a jammed mesh is visible.

steps.label: THE RESULT
steps.text: CoordinationMessage lists senderId, sentAt and sequenceNumber again, and the diagram is as it was. Edits stay in this browser until you Save or Export.

steps.label: INTERCONNECTION VIEW
steps.text: Interconnection is for parts and their connections, and Common has neither. It shows the 25 items declared inside its ports and definitions, unconnected.

steps.label: REQUIREMENT VIEW
steps.text: Common's 22 require constraints: 12 hold a measure of effectiveness to its target, 10 hold a budget that the brief fixes.

steps.label: READ ONE CONSTRAINT
steps.text: Select one and zoom in to read it: areaUnderWatchTarget, areaUnderWatchFraction ≥ 0.9, at least 0.9 of the area under watch at any moment. Each box shows its condition.

steps.label: PARAMETRIC VIEW
steps.text: Parametric is where values are bound to constraints, with the Bind tool. Common binds none, so it shows the same 22 constraints, each with its condition, standing alone.

outro.title: OA — Operational analysis
outro.text: How the tasked area is watched and reported today, before any system is named. The live model: cosmindxu.github.io/mbse-workflow
